anchor.quote: $m = \lceil n/b \rceil$ is the number of digits in each input
The radix is $Q_0 = 2^b$, the number of values a digit can take
The index $t$ runs over the positions
whose output is the list of integer coefficients $c_0, c_1, \dots$
The digit $d_t$ is the $t$th base-$Q_0$ digit of the output
The carry $e_t$ is the amount carried into position $t$ from the lower positions
$\tau$ counts the low positions already processed
where $w \bmod Q_0$ is the remainder of $w$ on division by $Q_0$

gaps.term: the paper's choice of digit width
gaps.quote: The paper uses this choice for large $n$
gaps.note: The page attributes the choice b = ceil(log_2 n) to an unnamed paper and gives no source. The reader cannot check that claim from the page. The consequence Q_0 >= n does follow from b = ceil(log_2 n).

gaps.quote: Since $m \le n \le Q_0$, this is below $Q_0^3$
gaps.note: m = ceil(n/b) <= n needs b >= 1, that is n >= 2, which the page never states. The reader cannot check m <= n from the page.
